lede: Class labels bring spread near the real images. PatchGAN’s digits grid is still two glyphs. Feature matching keeps a loss above BCE.
title: Conditional GAN, PatchGAN, and feature matching
question: Does a class label, a PatchGAN discriminator, or feature matching change quality and diversity?
process: Six runs share one recipe: 250 train and 50 test images per class, 40 epochs, 10 classes, noise 64, hidden 256, Adam with lr 0.0002 and β1 0.5. The variants are cGAN, PatchGAN, and feature matching, each on digits and on Fashion. Feature matching adds fm_weight 10 times an L1 feature term to generator BCE. On the other two variants, generator loss equals generator BCE. The spread ratio is scored sample std divided by real std. Vanilla ratios use the previous chapter’s test files. reports/mnist_gan_extensions/evaluation_test.json and best_params.json are the cGAN digits mirror. The six comparison numbers come from experiments/<variant>/<dataset>/evaluation_test.json.

opening.summary: Vanilla digits and Fashion sit near 0.09 and 0.08, and both collapse. All six extension runs land between 0.93 and 1.12, and every score file sets mode_collapse to false. The class grids are the part that still fails.

marks.label: Feature matching, Fashion
marks.summary: Feature matching on Fashion is scored. Generator loss 7.41 against BCE 2.71. Spread is 0.727 / 0.647 = 1.123, diversity 0.656, class separation 0.693. The grid has speckled garments and a few rows that do not hold a shape. best_params.json and the mirrored evaluation_test.json still name the cGAN digits run, which is the archive the DVC paths point at.

reflection.worked: Conditioning on the class label is the change that shows up in the spread number on both datasets. All six runs sit between 0.93 and 1.12 and set mode_collapse to false. cGAN digits reaches 1.047, and most rows of its class grid are a different digit. Feature matching is visible in the loss: generator loss stays well above BCE on digits (6.54 vs 2.98) and on Fashion (7.41 vs 2.71).
reflection.unexpected: PatchGAN digits scores 1.049 and then draws two glyphs. The collapse flag misses that, because two crisp shapes still have a large pixel standard deviation. Sharpness tells a different story: PatchGAN is closest to real ink (0.387 vs 0.256 on digits, 0.419 vs 0.301 on Fashion), while cGAN stays speckled (0.628 and 0.698). Fashion rows are not uniformly clothes. Several are noise.
reflection.why: A class target stops the generator from parking every noise vector on one image. It does not force ten classes, and it does not force pen ink. PatchGAN can satisfy a local patch with a sharp edge, then repeat that edge. Feature matching adds a second generator term, which is why its loss is not comparable to the BCE-only curves. The extension slice is 250 images per class and the vanilla slice is 400, so the spread chart compares finished runs, not a matched ablation.
reflection.improve: Judge a run on the class grid and on sharpness against real sharpness, not on spread alone and not on whether generator loss went down. PatchGAN’s cleaner edges are the sharpness win, and its digits grid is the failure. Feature matching already logs BCE beside the full generator loss. The open gap is the Fashion rows that are still noise, and cGAN sharpness of 0.628 against real digits at 0.256.
